english: get involved with; have to do with
use: Often a warning: 'Aitsu to wa kakawaranai hou ga ii' (Better not get mixed up with him).

example.romaji: Ano hito to wa amari kakawaranai hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: あの人とはあまり関わらない方がいいよ。
example.english: Better not get too involved with that person.

examplePolite.romaji: Ano hito to wa amari kakawaranai hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの人とはあまり関わらない方がいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: It's better not to get too involved with that person.

notes: Also 'be a matter of': 'inochi ni kakawaru' (life-threatening).

use: Mostly heard as kirawareru (be disliked): 'Kirawareta kamo' (Maybe they hate me now).

example.ja: 彼に嫌われたかもしれない。

examplePolite.ja: 彼に嫌われたかもしれません。

notes: To say you dislike something yourself, kirai da is far more common than kirau.

use: For avoiding people, topics or crowds; sakerareru means 'be avoided'.

example.romaji: Saikin, nanka sakerareteru ki ga suru.
example.ja: 最近、なんか避けられてる気がする。
example.english: Lately I feel like I'm being avoided.

examplePolite.romaji: Saikin, sakerarete iru ki ga shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 最近、避けられている気がします。
examplePolite.english: Lately I feel like I'm being avoided.

notes: Also physically dodging something, like a ball or a puddle.

english: pay attention to, fuss over; mind
use: 'Kamatte' asks for attention; 'Kamawanaide' means 'Leave me alone'.

example.ja: 猫が構ってほしいみたい。
example.english: The cat seems to want some attention.

examplePolite.romaji: Neko ga kamatte hoshii mitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 猫が構ってほしいみたいです。
examplePolite.english: The cat seems to want some attention.

notes: The 'mind' sense lives in the negative: kamawanai, kamaimasen (I don't mind).

use: Casually shortened to hottoku: 'Hottoite!' (Leave me alone!).

example.ja: もういいから、ほっといて。
example.english: Just forget it and leave me alone.

examplePolite.romaji: Mou kekkou desu kara, houtte oite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: もう結構ですから、放っておいてください。
examplePolite.english: That's enough, please just leave me alone.

notes: Also leaving a problem untouched: 'Houtte oku to waruku naru' (It'll get worse if you leave it).

use: Mostly shin'you dekiru / dekinai (can / can't trust) and 'Shin'you shite' (Trust me).

example.romaji: Ano hito no koto, mada shin'you dekinai.
example.ja: あの人のこと、まだ信用できない。
example.english: I still can't trust that person.

examplePolite.romaji: Ano hito no koto wa, mada shin'you dekimasen.
examplePolite.ja: あの人のことは、まだ信用できません。
examplePolite.english: I still can't trust that person.

notes: Shin'you is trusting someone's word or track record; shinrai is deeper trust in the person.

use: Deep trust in someone's character or ability, usually in -te iru.

example.romaji: Kare no koto wa shinrai shiteru kara daijoubu.
example.ja: 彼のことは信頼してるから大丈夫。
example.english: I trust him, so it's fine.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare no koto wa shinrai shite imasu kara, daijoubu desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼のことは信頼していますから、大丈夫です。
examplePolite.english: I trust him, so it's fine.

notes: The noun is common too: 'shinrai o ushinau' (lose someone's trust).

example.romaji: Chichi no koto, hontou ni sonkei shiteru.
example.ja: 父のこと、本当に尊敬してる。
example.english: I really look up to my dad.

examplePolite.romaji: Chichi no koto wa hontou ni sonkei shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 父のことは本当に尊敬しています。
examplePolite.english: I truly look up to my father.

notes: Sonkei is respect for someone you know; akogareru is admiring from a distance.

english: look up to, admire; long for
use: The person or thing takes ni; often a dream of being like someone or living somewhere.

example.romaji: Kodomo no koro, pairotto ni akogareteta.
example.ja: 子供の頃、パイロットに憧れてた。
example.english: As a kid, I dreamed of being a pilot.

examplePolite.romaji: Kodomo no koro, pairotto ni akogarete imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 子供の頃、パイロットに憧れていました。
examplePolite.english: As a child, I dreamed of being a pilot.

notes: The noun akogare is someone or something you dream of; it can be crush-like admiration.

english: be convinced, accept; be satisfied (with a reason)
use: Mostly 'nattoku dekinai' (I can't accept that) and 'nattoku shita' (Now it makes sense).

example.romaji: Sono setsumei ja nattoku dekinai yo.
example.ja: その説明じゃ納得できないよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Sono setsumei de wa nattoku dekimasen.
examplePolite.ja: その説明では納得できません。

use: For making a call on the facts: 'Jibun de handan shite' (Use your own judgment).

example.romaji: Sore wa jibun de handan shite yo.
example.ja: それは自分で判断してよ。
example.english: You'll have to decide that for yourself.

examplePolite.romaji: Sore wa jibun de handan shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: それは自分で判断してください。

notes: The noun is common too: 'ii handan' (a good call), 'handan ga muzukashii' (it's hard to say).

use: 'Gokai da yo!' means 'You've got it wrong!'; 'Gokai shinaide' means 'Don't get the wrong idea'.

example.romaji: Chigau yo, sore wa gokai da yo.
example.ja: 違うよ、それは誤解だよ。
example.english: No, you've got the wrong idea.

examplePolite.ja: 違います、それは誤解です。

notes: Also gokai suru (misunderstand) and gokai sareru (be misunderstood).

use: For a muddled head or a chaotic situation: 'Atama ga konran shiteru' (My head's spinning).

example.romaji: Chotto matte, atama ga konran shiteru.
example.ja: ちょっと待って、頭が混乱してる。
example.english: Hang on, my head's all mixed up.

examplePolite.romaji: Chotto matte kudasai, atama ga konran shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと待ってください、頭が混乱しています。

notes: Also public chaos, as with traffic or markets. For a light 'I'm lost', wakaranaku natta is more everyday.
